biography.plain_text: David Edward “Dave” Ritchie is a Canadian entrepreneur and co-founder of Ritchie Bros. Auctioneers. Beginning with a family furniture store in Kelowna, he helped turn a loan-repayment auction into an unreserved industrial-auction model. He later led its worldwide expansion, serving as chief executive and chairman before retiring from the board in 2006.

long_biography.plain_text:
A bank payment transformed David Ritchie's working life in 1958. He and his brothers needed to raise money for their Kelowna furniture store, so they sold surplus stock at an auction without reserve prices. The sale covered the debt and exposed a business opportunity. Five years later, a major road-building equipment auction persuaded them to leave furniture behind and concentrate on industrial machinery.

Ritchie became the driving force behind the company's expansion across Canada, into the United States and eventually overseas. He preserved the unreserved format and a culture of fair customer treatment while encouraging remote video auctions and an early equipment website. After decades at the helm, he retired from the board in 2006 and became chairman emeritus. The marketplace continued under professional management, carrying forward the auction principles he and his brothers established.

uncertainties.detail: David Ritchie is a common name and searches return unrelated athletes, clergy, academics and U.S. businesspeople. Exact-name SEC filings, the Edward middle name, Canadian identity, 1936 age alignment and consistent Kelowna/Ritchie Bros. history establish the founder identity; no namesake facts were imported.

Two strong biographies establish a 1936 birth in Kelowna, and the year matches both the company's age statement and the immutable calculated age. A local article gives March 2, but that exact day and month lacked equally strong independent corroboration, so only birth year, place and country are proposed.

Ritchie did not begin from a blank slate: he and his brothers received their father's modest second-hand furniture store. They then created the unreserved-auction model and transformed the operation into an international industrial business. Mixed records both the inter vivos family transfer and the separately documented founder-led expansion without implying inherited wealth at scale.

Ritchie retired from the chief executive role in 2004 and from the board in 2006. Later company material confirms that he has long ceased to manage Ritchie Bros. Historical filings mention private real estate and former company shareholdings, but reliable current evidence does not establish a dominant present sector or portfolio, so primary industry is Unknown.

No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia page or personal website could be identity-verified through an official cross-link or two independent high-specificity sources. The RB Global Hall of Fame page is retained as evidence rather than misclassified as a personal social profile.

The biographies exclude all current and historical vessel facts, point-in-time net worth and share values, current company transaction metrics, politics, controversy, legal matters and sensitive personal information. Nothing has been compiled or applied.
